properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: hash.js@1.1.7 is the SHA-family hash library (SHA-1/SHA-224/256/384/512) in the foundry workspace's dependency tree (pulled by web3/ethereumjs tooling). Available in the shipped build; SHA-1 usage would be collision-broken, SHA-2 usage is fine — the package provides both.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: sha1@0.10.6 is the Rust SHA-1 crate declared in the alloy-rust Cargo.lock — collision-broken hash available in the shipped Rust dependency tree (dep of the Rust crypto stack). Presence inventory: no direct call site confirmed in first-party .rs code.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: secp256k1 is the workhorse curve of this repo's whole web3 toolchain: declared as secp256k1@4.0.3 / @noble/secp256k1@1.7.1 / tiny-secp256k1 dependencies, and live at crypto.createECDH('secp256k1') in the javascript-cryptography demo (confirmed op-chain: secrets computed at ECDH.jsx:54/64) and as the ecc library wired into bitcoinjs for Taproot/BIP340 signing (BTC/Advanced/Taproot/example/index.js:4,7). Quantum-unsafe under Shor, but the curve is fixed by the Bitcoin/Ethereum protocols themselves

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Hardcoded secp256k1 private keys in plaintext: 10 keys as LOCAL_RICH_WALLETS in the zkSync deploy helper (deterministic in-memory-node test accounts, well-known in zksync docs), plus wallet-test.js:15 and makerdao-multicall.js:4. Real hardcoded key material — worthless on a local dev node, catastrophic if the pattern is copied to a live network, and the deterministic rich-wallet keys are publicly known so any funds sent to those addresses on a real chain are instantly stealable. Changeable here:

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: evp_bytestokey@1.0.3 implements OpenSSL's legacy EVP_BytesToKey — a single-round MD5-based KDF with no salt by default — dragged into the foundry workspace by the browserify crypto stack that web3 tooling depends on. Weak-KDF capability present in the shipped dependency tree; worth flagging because any code that routes through browserify-aes inherits it. Changeable here (dependency pin).

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Hardcoded IV literal inside the embedded Web3 secret-storage v3 keystore fixture in the ethers.js wallet tutorial — the blob is live-decrypted by ethers.Wallet.fromEncryptedJson (password "foo"); IV is fixed because the whole keystore is sample data. A real keystore write generates a fresh IV per file per the standard. Fixture-grade but a genuine static-IV sighting; changeable by regenerating sample keystores.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: node-forge@1.3.1 declared in the frontend package-lock (pulled via selfsigned@2.1.1, itself a react-scripts dev-server dependency): ships RSA public-key encryption (PKCS#1 v1.5/OAEP) — Shor-vulnerable. Presence-level inventory; no RSA call site found in the application code. node-forge 1.3.1 predates the 2024 CVE fixes for its RSA PKCS#1 v1.5 forgery class.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: k256@0.13.3 (RustCrypto secp256k1) declared in alloy-rust's Cargo.lock at line 2244 — the ECDSA engine behind alloy's Ethereum transaction/account signing. Transitive dep of the alloy toolchain; no direct call site in the crate's own src. Shor-vulnerable signature (deadline risk, not harvest); migration ML-DSA-65, though secp256k1 is fixed by the Ethereum protocol for on-chain verification.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: utility.getRandomInt in the vendored EtherDelta backup: Math.random()-based integer helper — CWE-338-pattern weak randomness. Defined but never called anywhere in this tree (dead code), so no live security impact today; must never back order IDs/nonces/tokens if ever wired up. Changeable here.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: secp256k1 declared in the Circle CCTP toolchain's lockfile (via @noble/curves / viem) — the curve viem uses for the wallet clients that sign CCTP burn/approve transactions in src/usdc_transfer_cctp.ts. Quantum-unsafe; curve fixed by the EVM protocol.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: aes-128-ctr is the Web3 secret-storage v3 standard cipher for Ethereum keystores; this fixture is live-decrypted by ethers.Wallet.fromEncryptedJson and wallet.encrypt() emits the same format. The keystore's keccak256 MAC authenticates the ciphertext, so CTR malleability is mitigated inside this construction. Cipher fixed by the Ethereum keystore standard.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: The repo's one live ECDH implementation: the javascript-cryptography React demo runs crypto.createECDH('secp256k1') at module scope with generateKeys() and computeSecret() on button click — a real secp256k1 key agreement, Shor-vulnerable (B-). Six App.jsx sites were rejected as UI route/menu labels; the component, its export wiring and the with-hardhat lockfile dependency (elliptic/secp256k1-class packages) carry the asset. Changeable here; ML-KEM-768 is the replacement.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Ed25519 is provided by ring@0.17.13 (its Ed25519 implementation) across the Rust and JS dependency trees of this repo's blockchain tooling — available in the shipped build; no direct Ed25519 call site found in first-party app code. Quantum-unsafe signature (Shor → ML-DSA-65), changeable at the dependency level when the toolchain moves.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: ECDSA (secp256k1) is the wallet authentication type selected for zkSync Era cross-L2 transfers (ethAuthType: "ECDSA" in L2ToL2transfer.js) and the signature algorithm every ethers/@noble dependency in the foundry lockfile provides. Quantum-unsafe (Shor); migration is an ecosystem decision (ML-DSA-65), not a repo-local one.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: X25519 is declared via ring@0.17.13 (its X25519 agreement) in the alloy-rust Cargo.lock and reachable through the foundry pnpm workspace — the ECDH curve TLS stacks negotiate for key exchange. Quantum-unsafe under Shor (harvest-now-decrypt-later for any TLS traffic); replaceable only by moving the TLS layer to a hybrid X25519+ML-KEM-768 group, which depends on the runtime (OpenSSL 3.5+/Node 24) the toolchain links. Observable here at the dependency level.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: P-256 (secp256r1) declared in the circle-cctp lockfile via @noble/curves — NIST-curve ECDSA/ECDH capability available in the shipped build (viem pulls the whole curves bundle). Quantum-unsafe (Shor); changeable at the dependency level when viem ships PQ curves.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Keccak-256 (Ethereum's pre-standard SHA-3 variant, different padding from FIPS SHA-3) is the workhorse hash across this Web3 tutorial repo. All 75 sites reviewed: live ethers/eth-util/Web3 keccak256 + solidityKeccak256 calls — access-control role IDs, event-topic selectors, EIP-712 typed-data hashing, EIP-7702 authorization hashes, Merkle-tree leaves for airdrops, CREATE2 address derivation, ECDSA message hashes — plus keccak@3.0.4/@ethersproject/keccak256@5.7.0/keccak256@1.0.2 dependency declar

properties.name: pqs:context

Iteration counts are chosen by callers (ethers uses 2048 for keystores historically); capability present in the shipped tree.

properties.name: pqs:context
